title: Carry a stack of three boxes onto a shelf in one trip, squeezed between both arms
instruction: Move the stack of three boxes onto the shelf in one go, keeping them stacked the whole time: do not lift any box off the one below it.
context: Moving house or unpacking a delivery, people carry a short stack of boxes in one trip by squeezing the bottom box from both sides while the boxes above ride on it. The bottom box is wider than one gripper opens, so both arms must hold it. Unlike TK-4E4YZF (one wide box squeezed and lifted) and pilots TK-CTCQVY and TK-TH7NBJ (carries of one object), the hard part here is keeping two loose boxes on top in place through the squeeze, lift, carry and set-down.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Boxes (loose, light-to-mid brown cardboard, modelled as solid rigid blocks): bottom box 200 mm wide (left to right), 120 mm deep (front to back) and 50 mm tall, 120 g; middle box 120 x 120 mm and 35 mm tall, 60 g; top box 80 x 80 mm and 30 mm tall, 40 g. They stand in one stack, edges square to the table, each box centred on the one below, the stack's centre 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline: the bottom box spans 14.0 to 26.0 cm in front of the bases and 10 cm either side of the midline. The stack's top is 115 mm high. Shelf (fixed, grey painted wood, a solid block): 160 mm deep, 240 mm wide and 60 mm tall, spanning 29.0 to 45.0 cm in front of the bases and 12 cm either side of the midline, so its front face is 30 mm beyond the bottom box's far face. The gripper opens to at most 94 mm between its pads, less than either footprint side of the bottom box. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a photo, and judged over the whole trial. Every limit below is inclusive (a value exactly at a limit passes). A box is flat when its top face is within 5 degrees of level, either way up (a box turned upside down counts as flat, one on its side does not); at rest means moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s. A box rests on a surface when its lowest corner is within 1 mm of that surface (for an upper box, of the top of the box below); an upper box's offset is the horizontal distance between its centre and the centre of the box below it. The stack is broken, and the trial scores 0 whatever happens afterwards, if at any moment the middle box's lowest corner is more than 5 mm above the bottom box's top or the top box's lowest corner is more than 5 mm above the middle box's top, an offset exceeds 25 mm, or any box tilts more than 15 degrees (so carrying boxes one at a time, or lifting the upper boxes off and putting them back, scores 0). The stack is standing when all three boxes are flat and at rest, the middle box rests on the bottom box and the top box rests on the middle box. Score 1.0: the stack was never broken, the bottom box rests on the shelf top with all four of its bottom corners over the shelf top (no overhang), and the stack is standing with both offsets at most 10 mm. Score 0.5: the stack was never broken, the bottom box rests on the shelf top with its centre over the shelf top, and the stack is standing with both offsets at most 25 mm, but the bottom box overhangs an edge of the shelf or an offset is over 10 mm. Score 0.25: the stack was never broken, it was lifted as one at some moment in the trial (the bottom box's lowest corner at least 20 mm above the table), and it now stands on the table (bottom box resting on the table) with both offsets at most 25 mm and the bottom box's centre at least 30 mm from where it started. Score 0 in every other case: the stack left where it was or slid along the table without being lifted, held more than 1 mm above the shelf, any box on the table or knocked off, or the stack broken at any time. Scoring looks only at the boxes, so a stack resting fully on the shelf (or, for 0.25, on the table) counts whether or not the grippers are still holding it. Setting the stack down and taking a new grip is allowed, as long as the stack is never broken. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step. The record of the trial (broken, lifted) starts afresh only on a scene reset: all three boxes within 0.5 mm and 1 degree (any rotation) of their starting poses and at rest, having got there by a jump of more than 20 mm in one control step; restacking the boxes at the start by hand does not clear it.
reset_notes: Restack the three boxes at the start position, edges square to the table, each centred on the one below. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. The boxes are solid rigid blocks of the stated mass, smaller than moving boxes, with no flaps, contents or give, and rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 sliding), well above cardboard's, so upper boxes slide less than real ones. The upper boxes are narrower than the bottom one, so a squeeze on its sides leaves them free; the closed fingers widen upward, so the scripted squeeze presses on its top edges. The shelf is a solid block.
